digest_title: Daily Security Digest: Vulnerability Boundaries and System Hardening
dek: A daily briefing covering critical vulnerabilities, supply chain controls, agent isolation, and defensive runtime hardening.
overview: Today's advisories highlight critical boundaries in static file handling, memory management, protocol parsers, and access controls. Across open-source packages, enterprise platforms, and routers, proper version proof, object-level authorization, and runtime isolation remain the definitive controls for risk reduction.

stories.headline: Restify Static Files Need Filesystem Boundaries
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90494 affects Restify's serveStatic handler up to version 12.0.0, introducing a remotely reachable path-traversal weakness.
stories.why_it_matters: Configuration determines exposure; teams must inventory routes and enforce filesystem least privilege.

stories.headline: S2OPC Flaw Makes Resource Headroom a Boundary
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90782 describes a null-pointer dereference in S2OPC up to version 1.7.3 under specific allocation failure conditions.
stories.why_it_matters: Memory-exhaustion handling is a security boundary that determines whether services fail safely.

stories.headline: CrewAI Code Execution Needs an Outer Boundary
stories.summary: CVE-2026-37008 exposes CrewAI versions before commit fb2323b to alternative import-time module execution paths.
stories.why_it_matters: Isolation must not silently weaken when dependencies are unavailable; execution boundaries must fail closed.

stories.headline: ESPnet Model Checkpoints Need a Load Boundary
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90777 affects ESPnet versions before 202609 through unsafe deserialization in pretrained checkpoint loading paths.
stories.why_it_matters: Model files cross from data into computation at load time, requiring restricted loading.

stories.headline: Rhymix File References Need Object-Level Authorization
stories.summary: CVE-2026-36453 affects Rhymix versions before 2.1.31 through an insecure direct object reference in custom fields.
stories.why_it_matters: Server-side object binding is required to ensure file actions re-establish user authority.

stories.headline: YouTube Embed Flaw Turns Plugin Retirement Into Control
stories.summary: CVE-2026-88793 affects YouTube Embed versions 10.0 through 10.3 with unauthenticated stored cross-site scripting.
stories.why_it_matters: Abandoned plugins with no fixed releases require removal and content review to eliminate risk.

stories.headline: MKVToolNix Flaw Makes Media Intake a Parser Boundary
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90783 describes a heap buffer overflow in AVI-reading code bundled with MKVToolNix through version 101.0.
stories.why_it_matters: Files are structured instructions to parsers, requiring strict intake isolation and provenance controls.

stories.headline: Hoo Companion Import Flaw Makes Settings a Boundary
stories.summary: CVE-2026-85129 exposes Hoo Companion 1.0.2 to unauthenticated theme-settings import and stored cross-site scripting.
stories.why_it_matters: Configuration integrity requires plugin removal and verification of state from known-good sources.

stories.headline: Orion-Visor Default Key Needs Deployment-Level Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90510 exposes Orion-Visor versions 2.5.0 through 2.5.7 to a shared encryption-key fallback in configuration.
stories.why_it_matters: Control planes require proof that each deployment uses a unique secret rather than defaults.

stories.headline: BioStar AD Credential Fix Needs Service-Account Boundaries
stories.summary: CVE-2026-31278 discloses Active Directory bind credentials through an API response in BioStar 2 before 2.9.12.
stories.why_it_matters: Connector credentials require application updates, immediate secret rotation, and least-privilege scoping.

stories.headline: Apache Doris Fix Needs Query-Level Access Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-68570 allows authenticated users to bypass privilege checks and read unauthorized data in Apache Doris.
stories.why_it_matters: Database permissions require query-level tests of denied paths to ensure enforcement integrity.

stories.headline: Internet Download Manager Driver Flaw Demands Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90493 affects Internet Download Manager kernel drivers on Windows through version 6.42 Build 63.
stories.why_it_matters: Application names are poor proxies for kernel risk; teams must verify the exact driver loaded.

stories.headline: New DIR-878 Flaws Make Router Retirement the Fix
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90692 and CVE-2026-90693 affect D-Link DIR-878 firmware version 120B05 with stack-based buffer overflows.
stories.why_it_matters: End-of-life edge equipment requires asset retirement rather than waiting for unsupported patches.

stories.headline: Memcached Fix Needs Protocol-Path Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90698 describes an out-of-bounds read in memcached versions 1.6.41 through 1.6.43 during authenticated ASCII paths.
stories.why_it_matters: Parser flaws require live process verification to ensure daemons have crossed the fixed boundary.

stories.headline: New DWR-M920 Flaw Needs Firmware-Level Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-90699 describes command injection in D-Link DWR-M920 firmware version 1.1.7.
stories.why_it_matters: Hardware revisions and regional firmware numbering require explicit vendor validation before safety is assumed.

stories.headline: ACME Validation Needs a Network Boundary
stories.summary: CVE-2026-18369 affects Red Hat Certificate System 10.4, allowing ACME responder SSRF through IP-literal identifiers.
stories.why_it_matters: Validation services with privileged network placement must strictly govern all destination requests.

stories.headline: Microsoft's AI Guardrails Need Runtime Proof
stories.summary: Microsoft's draft MAI code of conduct establishes non-negotiable agent constraints, tool scopes, and minimum privileges.
stories.why_it_matters: Written behavior is not deployed assurance; organizations must enforce boundaries in underlying systems.

operating_view: Treat software inventories, package metadata, and vendor documentation as discovery signals rather than definitive proof of runtime safety. Enforce strict filesystem, memory, network, and object-level boundaries across every deployed asset.
watch_items: Verify running binary versions and active drivers rather than relying on package manager states.
Enforce strict egress controls and network boundaries around services that process untrusted inputs.
Validate privilege separation and object authorization across all custom fields and agent tools.
caption_intro: Review today's security briefing detailing critical vulnerabilities, container isolation requirements, and infrastructure boundary hardening across multiple software ecosystems.
